name: Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı)
description: Subterranean cathedral-sized water reservoir supported by 336 marble columns, capable of storing 80,000 cubic meters of fresh water.
history: Filtered water from the Belgrade Forest for the Great Palace of Constantinople and the imperial court.
construction: Built with waterproof Roman brick-and-mortar masonry and repurposed classical columns, including two famous Medusa head bases.
architecture: Features 12 rows of 28 Corinthian and Ionic marble columns rising nine meters from the brick floor under vaulted brick cross-arches.
significance: Masterpiece of Byzantine civil and hydraulic engineering.
currentStatus: Open to the public as a museum in Istanbul, Turkey.
